newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors seek arrest of two bankers.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors seek arrest of two bankers.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Wednesday asked a Seoul court to issue warrants for the arrest of the heads of two leading banks in connection with loans to Hanbo Steel Co, a prosecution official said.
He said the warrants were being sought for Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank and Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung Bank on charges of bribery.

Prosecution officials have been questioning Sheen, Woo and Lee Hyung-koo, the former head of the state-run Korea Development Bank, on whether they received commissions in return for offering huge loans to Hanbo Steel, the country's second largest steelmaker.
The official did not say whether prosecutors were considering any action against Lee.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group, the 14th-largest conglomerate in South Korea, had accumulated about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
Prosecutors last Friday arrested Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo on charges of fraud, illegally issuing cheques and violating laws on trust and savings companies.
